title: Multi-tenant streaming chat load synthesizer with adaptive token pacing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Build a reusable, multi-tenant streaming load synthesizer that more accurately models real-world SSE/WebSocket chat traffic for Redwood inference. The harness should exercise token-level throughput (tokens/sec), p95 end-to-end token latency, KV-cache warmup behavior, and graceful client churn/backpressure. Goals: 1) Provide reproducible regression detection (statistical baselines + drift detection) for p95 token latencies across commits and model variants. 2) Support configurable tenant mixes, message size distributions, persona/role selection, and intermittent KV-cache priming. 3) Integrate with CI and our observability stack to block regressions above configurable thresholds. Non-goals: full synthetic UI workload replay (we focus on protocol-level fidelity and tokenflow).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 5k concurrent simulated streams across SSE and WebSocket protocols with configurable client mixes
Reports token/sec, per-request p50/p95/p99 for both generation-time and end-to-end latency in a format ingestible by Grafana/Influx
Regression detection pipeline (baseline + drift) flags >2% p95 regressions and emits alerts to #perf-alerts and GitHub check
Supports KV-cache warmup scenarios (cold, warm, primed) and includes a warmup phase in each run
Deterministic replay mode for reproducing flagged regressions and an exportable artifact (trace IDs + input prompts)
steps: Design input distribution model (client mix, message length, model variant mapping) - doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-streaming-load-model
Implement session generator with protocol shim supporting SSE and WebSocket and token-level pacing jitter
Add KV-cache priming layer that can pin prefixes and simulate cache hit rates
Instrument per-token timing hooks and event traces to emit to our tracing pipeline (Zipkin/Grafana)
Create regression detector job that compares recent runs against baseline histograms and outputs a summary JSON
Integrate with CI: add GitHub Action to run a lightweight smoke harness on PRs and full run scheduled nightly
Wire alerts to #perf-alerts and create a GitHub check that can block merges when thresholds are exceeded
comments: 2025-01-20 - Ava Martinez: Kicked off design doc; sketched distribution model. Decided to prioritize jittered token pacing over trying to perfectly replay SDK client timings to keep harness lightweight.
2025-01-25 - Jared Thompson: Prototype session generator accepts a JSON workload spec. Early tests show we can sustain 2k streams per node with current client config (needs tuning).
2025-01-28 - Performance SIG review: Agreed on baseline approach using histogram comparison + Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for drift. Action: add configurable sensitivity levels (lenient/standard/strict).

2025-02-02 - QA: Found intermittent flakiness when simulating high churn over WebSocket; suspected connection re-use logic in proxy. Filed follow-up ENG-903457 for proxy connection pool investigation.
2025-02-05 - Jared Thompson: Implemented KV priming phase and per-token timing instrumentation. P95 sample from nightly run attached to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/184
2025-02-07 - Design feedback from Priya Rao: Recommend adding a tenant isolation knob (simulate noisy neighbors) and an option to pin specific model variants per tenant. Will add to next iteration.

2025-02-09 - Ava Martinez: Added Grafana dashboard prototype (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming-load/streaming-chat-load) and hooked CI smoke job. Next: finalize alert thresholds and add GitHub check integration.
notes: Trade-offs: We are choosing statistical regression detection (histogram drift) instead of delta-based thresholds because it generalizes across different token distributions and model sizes.

Operational concern: Running full-scale nightly runs (100k tokens/sec sustained) will require scheduling on dedicated test fleets; plan to use burst capacity in Dedicated test org to avoid noisy neighbor impact on production clusters.
Follow-ups: Create a reproducible incident playbook for when the harness flags regressions in production (owner, rollback steps, data collection checklist).
